Theme

Time, the calendar & feasts

schedule verb

fix a day or time for something

also scheduled, schedule a meeting, fix a date, set a date, as scheduled, on the scheduled day, appointed day

classical

Caes. BG 1.47.1: conloquiō diem cōnstitueret
Caes. BG 1.30: diem conciliō (Lewis & Short)

cōnstituō, cōnstituere, cōnstituī, cōnstitūtum

verb, third conjugation: <span lang="la">diem</span> + dative of the event

fix, appoint (a day for something)

The day goes in the accusative and the event in the dative: diem conloquiō cōnstituere, to schedule a meeting. Agreed with someone: cum aliquō cōnstituere (Cic. Verr. 2.2.65, Lewis & Short). As scheduled: ut erat cōnstitūtum (Cic. Clu. 37, Lewis & Short); on the scheduled day, diē cōnstitūtā (Caes. BG 1.4.2). The noun schedule, a timetable, is hōrārium (see schedule).

Examples

  • utī aut iterum conloquiō diem cōnstitueret aut, sī id minus vellet, ex suīs lēgātīs aliquem ad sē mitteret

    (he asked) that Caesar should either fix a day for another meeting or, if he did not want that, send him one of his officersCaes. BG 1.47.1

  • Diē cōnstitūtā causae dictiōnis Orgetorīx ad jūdicium omnem suam familiam, ad hominum mīlia decem, undique coēgit

    On the day fixed for his trial Orgetorix gathered his whole household at the court, some ten thousand men, from all sidesCaes. BG 1.4.2

See also schedule, deadline, organise, agree.

SourcesLewis & Short: constituo
